status: authored 2026-10-02, not yet applied to any world
owner_request: The owner, 2026-10-02, standing on the summit in staging looking at Articuno's tower: "there should be some foliage and something else up here." Their screenshot: a smooth bare snow dome about 110 blocks across, the tower alone in the middle, clouds below.
purpose: Make Frostpeak's pressed summit read as a place without making it stop being 'a flat table of snow with the tower in the middle of it' (Dr. Halvard's words at the research camp, data/frostpeak_camp.json). One west wind explains everything placed here: it breaks rock through the snow at the exposed rim, plasters rime on the rocks' windward faces, and leaves a sheltered lee behind each rock where the only plants on the summit grow and a drift tails off. And the old pilgrims' way comes up the long west ridge into that wind and turns to the tower's north door, marked by cairns, some fallen.

story.chosen: the old pilgrims' way and the rime
story.why: The camp tells a player two things about the summit that a player cannot check from below: the tower is old ('a tower on the summit that nobody alive remembers being built'; 'nobody hauls stone up a mountain for nothing') and it is cold ('frost on the tower when the slopes are bare, a cold wind out of a clear sky'). The cairned way is the evidence for the first: people came here, long ago, and came to the door; half its cairns have been knocked down by the wind and nobody has rebuilt them. The rime is the evidence for the second, up close. The way also does a job: the camp sees the tower's south face, the door is on the north, and the way leads a player round to it.

rejected.researchers_traces: The camp's own dialogue says the survey has never stood on the summit: Krell knows where the table is only by theodolite ('That is how we know where the table is without seeing it') and Halvard has not seen the bird. A survey cairn or a cache up here would contradict them.
rejected.older_shrine_ruins: A second ruin beside a tower nobody remembers building says the same thing twice and competes with the tower for the eye.
rejected.lights: No lantern or light block: the summit is wilderness, not a town (docs/STATE.md 'Places are lit as towns'); it is dark by design.

story.never_promises: Nothing placed here refers to the altar, offers anything, gates anything or runs a command. Whether the LumyMon altar works and how a player gets its glacier feather are open owner decisions (data/adopted_legendary_sites.json still_gated_by; EXP-048).

ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/frostpeak_summit.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y except the tower door's sill, read from the template.

site.measured: 2026-10-02 from tools/ground.py: ground y310 at radius 50 and 60 on all 24 bearings (every 15 degrees) and y308..309 at 70, so the pressed table is flat to at least radius 60 everywhere; data/towns.json says 'flat within 55 blocks of the centre, feathered over 70'.

door.read_from: COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31.zip data/cobbleverse/structure/legendary/articuno.nbt, read 2026-10-02 with tools/structure_nbt.py load: template layer 0 is all structure void (no block entries), so the paste never touches ground y310; the entrance is three prismarine_brick_stairs facing south at template (9..11, 1, 3), flanked by stairs at (8, 1, 4) and (12, 1, 4), and the doorway is open at x9..11 z5..7 on layers 2 and 3. At the summit corner (672, 310, 369) that is the step at x681..683 z372 y311, entered walking south.

approach.rule: the straight 9-wide lane out of the door, from the tower box's north edge to z340: nothing stands above the ground in it; the way's flagstones and worn cells lie flush at ground level

camp_sightline.from: data/frostpeak_camp.json frostpeak_camp_telescope (the pivot and a player's eye on the deck beside it)
camp_sightline.to: the tower's box from y370 to its top layer: the part of the tower that clears the false crest from the camp (data/adopted_legendary_sites.json site.findable_by_eye)
camp_sightline.rule: no block this pack writes lies on any line from either viewpoint to that box

wind.basis: the map already has one: the repository's krummholz objects (tools/foliage_objects.py krummholz) stream their leaves to +x, so the wind that shaped Frostpeak's strand blows from the west. The summit gets the same wind: rime on the west faces, shelter, plants and drifts to the east.

table.why: Halvard promises 'a flat table of snow with the tower in the middle of it'. Inside radius 30 nothing grows and no rock breaks the snow; only the way crosses it.

tors.rule: Rock breaks through the snow only where the wind scours, on the rim: one tor per 30-degree slot round the table, between radius 40 and 54, its bearing and radius nudged by a hash of the slot (never random), each a repository boulder (tools/foliage_objects.py boulder, moss off) sunk one block into the ground. A slot is skipped when its tor, rime or lee would come within path_clearance of the way's centreline, within the tower's clearance, inside the bare table, onto another tor's cells, or past dress_radius (radius 60, where the measured table is still y310 on every bearing).
tors.sizes_note: (rx, ry, rz) for tools/foliage_objects.py boulder(): the library's six boulder shapes stretched upwards, so a tor stands one to four blocks over the snow, to be seen across the table

rime.rule: on the west face of a tor, one block thick, in front of a share of the rock cells above the ground; the share grows with the tor's exposure to the west wind: share = low + (high - low) * (1 + cos(bearing - 270)) / 2, bearing from the table's centre, so the west rim's tors are white-faced and the east rim's barely frosted

lee.rule: Behind each row of a tor (its blocks at one z), the lee reaches twice the row's height above the ground, at most reach_max. Cells are numbered d = 1, 2, ... east of the row's last rock block; each takes its band's soil and at most one plant, the plant chosen by a hash of the cell against the band's cumulative shares. The most sheltered cells carry the most and tallest plants; past the reach a drift tails off in snow layers. Nothing woody: the summit is y310 and the snowy_peak preset's treeline is y145 (data/regions.json), so the plants are the fellfield's herbs, ferns and moss.

way.rule: The pilgrims' way leaves the door straight north as a threshold of old flagstones, then runs straight to the rim at the arrival bearing: the bearing whose ground stays highest from 100 to 200 blocks out (the long gentle ridge a pilgrim would climb), searched every 5 degrees. Worn, not built: each cell's surface is chosen by a hash, and a share of cells is left under snow.

cairns.rule: Two gatepost cairns flank the threshold where it begins; then one every `spacing` blocks along the way, alternating sides, `offset` blocks from the centreline; every third is fallen, its stones strewn downwind (east) by the same wind; and a taller way-marker stands at the rim where the way arrives, seen from the ridge below.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only; none a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (azure bluet and the other flowers are, so no flower is used); nothing that emits light; no chest, bed or block entity

lighting.why: wilderness, not a town: no light is added (docs/STATE.md, 'Places are lit as towns ... the Scar and the jungle ruins are dark by design'). The tower's own sea lanterns are its light.

spawns.why: Frostpeak's surface table (data/spawns.json scope frostpeak) covers the summit; no block placed here is a spawn condition, so the dressing changes nothing about what spawns.

known_limits: Snow weather lays one snow layer over any bare cell (vanilla snowAccumulationHeight 1), so in time the worn way and the lee's soil can whiten; the rocks, rime, plants and cairns stand through it. NOT VERIFIED in game.

The export's surface block on the table is ASSUMED to be snow (data/regions.json snowy_peak terrain DEEP_SNOW above y165); the way and the lee replace the ground block itself, so they read the same whatever it is.
